producer_report.summary: Added the `athena-testutil` crate. `write_executable` writes the script to a temp name, closes it, sets mode 0755 and renames it into place. `run` and `retry_busy` retry while the error is ETXTBSY. All six listed test files now use it. I added D157 to docs/decisions.md, saying D08 was checked and stands, plus a matching `amended` link in docs/decision-links.toml. I also updated CHANGELOG.md and docs/architecture.md. One file outside the brief's list changed: xtask/shard-timings.txt, which a `ci_shards` test requires to list every test unit, so it needed two lines for the new crate. The rename alone does not remove the race, because the inode keeps its writer. The retry is what handles it, and the crate docs say so. I did not run the full workspace test suite. I ran the targeted tests and the policy scan instead (see checks_run).

open_issues: checks.rs and claude.rs tests start the stand-in inside the code under test, so they get the atomic write but no ETXTBSY retry.
xtask/shard-timings.txt is a changed file outside the brief's deliverables list; the timing values of 3.00 seconds for the new units are estimates.
mistakes: My first draft of the crate docs claimed the rename closes the race. It does not, so I rewrote the docs and made the stress test use `run`.
I left unused PermissionsExt imports in claude.rs and reconcile.rs; clippy caught them and I removed them.
learnings: xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs requires xtask/shard-timings.txt to list every workspace test unit, so a new crate with tests needs `<crate> --doc` and `<crate> --lib` lines there.
The decision link's `line` is the line of the "Amends Dxx" phrase in docs/decisions.md.
A rename keeps the inode, so a forked child's open write descriptor still blocks exec of the renamed file. Only a retry covers that window.
Bash in this environment rejects grep/tail; use the Grep and Read tools.
